data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's opening claim that 'Idempotence at the consumer/processing layer implies safety at the storage/log layer' is a non sequitur. Consumer-side idempotence (reprocessing the same event yields no additional state change) and storage-side safety (appending a duplicate does not violate structural invariants) are independent properties: you can have idempotent consumers over a corrupted log, or safe append-only storage with non-idempotent consumers. The log's structural safety is an intrinsic consequence of append-only semantics, not an implication of reader idempotence. This logical gap weakens the two-boundary model's foundation, since the claimed implication relationship between the boundaries does not hold.
